articles.title: ¿Un último baile juntos? En Millonarios responden sobre el regreso de Falcao junto a Cuadrado
articles.standfirst: Ariel Michaloutsos se refiere al posible regreso de Falcao al Embajador
articles.summary: Ariel Michaloutsos se refiere al posible regreso de Falcao al Embajador
articles.body: Luego de concretarse el fichaje de Juan Guillermo Cuadrado por parte de Millonarios, de inmediato surgió la inquietud entre la hinchada embajadora: ¿es posible ver de nuevo a Radamel Falcao García luciendo la camiseta azul al lado del atacante paisa? Cabe recordar que el vínculo del 'Tigre' de Santa Marta con el cuadro capitalino finalizó a mediados de este año. Sin embargo, la llegada de figuras de peso internacional al torneo local ha reavivado las conversaciones e ilusiones de volver a presenciar una dupla histórica en el campín. Frente a los rumores y solicitudes de la hinchada, la directiva albiazul se pronunció al respecto a través de su director deportivo, Ariel Michaloutsos. En entrevista con El Vbar Caracol, el dirigente aclaró el panorama inmediato y descartó la llegada del delantero para lo que resta de la temporada 2026-II debido a límites reglamentarios de la nómina. "Ya está el cupo de 25 jugadores inscritos. Ojalá que en enero él tenga todas las ganas", puntualizó Michaloutsos. De esta manera, aunque el regreso de Falcao queda descartado para el segundo semestre de 2026, la puerta queda entreabierta para una eventual vinculación a comienzos de 2027. La posibilidad de ver a ambos referentes de la Selección Colombia compartiendo camerino en Bogotá dependerá exclusivamente de la disposición del goleador samario para el próximo año. Juan Guillermo Cuadrado firmó un contrato que lo vincula con Millonarios hasta mediados de 2027, por lo que una eventual llegada de Falcao en el mercado de enero permitiría el ansiado cruce en el campo de juego. Hasta la fecha, Radamel Falcao no ha emitido confirmaciones oficiales sobre su futuro profesional ni ha anunciado un retiro definitivo, dejando abierta la expectativa en el entorno del fútbol colombiano. Mientras tanto, la hinchada embajadora aguarda por los próximos meses para saber si habrá un nuevo capítulo en la historia del 'Tigre' en la capital.

articles.title: Graves disturbios de los hinchas de Junior obligan a suspender el juego ante Alianza
articles.standfirst: Junior vs. Alianza suspendido por desmanes: ¿Qué pasó con la hinchada del tiburón en Valledupar?
articles.summary: Junior vs. Alianza suspendido por desmanes: ¿Qué pasó con la hinchada del tiburón en Valledupar?
articles.body: Un nuevo episodio de violencia empañó el desarrollo de la Liga BetPlay Dimayor. En el marco de la décima jornada del campeonato, el encuentro entre Alianza Fútbol Club y Junior de Barranquilla en el estadio Armando Maestre Pavajeau de Valledupar tuvo que ser suspendido de forma temporal debido a graves altercados en las graderías por parte de la hinchada visitante. El clima de tensión en el escenario deportivo comenzó a elevarse a medida que el conjunto barranquillero caía por la mínima diferencia (1-0) tras el tempranero gol de Ever Meza a los cuatro minutos de iniciado el juego. Con el paso de los minutos y ante la ineficacia del equipo dirigido por Sebastián Viera para revertir el marcador, un sector de la barra de Junior ubicado en la tribuna Oriental desató el caos. Cerca del minuto 80 de juego, varios aficionados procedieron a lanzar bengalas encendidas al terreno de juego e intentaron saltar las mallas de protección para invadir el campo e encarar a los futbolistas de la escuadra 'tiburona'. Ante el riesgo inminente para la integridad física de los deportistas y asistentes, el juez central Steven Camargo dio la orden de detener el partido. De inmediato, los jugadores de ambos planteles y el cuerpo arbitral abandonaron la cancha y se resguardaron en los camerinos. A pesar de que el partido contaba con un operativo de seguridad de 335 uniformados de la Policía Metropolitana de Valledupar, los desórdenes requirieron la intervención del ESMAD para controlar las agresiones contra la fuerza pública en las graderías. Tras aproximadamente 25 minutos de interrupción y luego de evacuar por completo la tribuna Oriental, las autoridades locales brindaron las garantías de seguridad necesarias para reanudar y culminar el encuentro. Tras el desalojo de la tribuna y el retorno de los equipos al césped, el marcador no sufrió modificaciones, confirmando la victoria 1-0 a favor de Alianza FC. Este resultado agrava aún más el momento crítico de Junior de Barranquilla en la liga, donde encadena una racha negativa de varios compromisos sin conocer la victoria. Al finalizar el choque, el técnico Sebastián Viera reconoció la falta de reacción de su plantel desde los primeros minutos, mientras las autoridades deportivas y la Dimayor evalúan posibles sanciones disciplinarias y de plaza tras los reprochables desmanes en territorio cesarense.

articles.title: La insólita multa a Sebastián Montoya por la vestimenta de su hermana Paulina en el Madring
articles.standfirst: Sebastián Montoya en la Fórmula 2: ¿Por qué lo multaron en Madrid por la ropa de su hermana?
articles.summary: Sebastián Montoya en la Fórmula 2: ¿Por qué lo multaron en Madrid por la ropa de su hermana?
articles.body: El piloto colombiano Sebastián Montoya, hijo del histórico exFórmula 1 Juan Pablo Montoya, vivió un episodio tan insólito como surrealista durante la jornada de clasificación en Madrid. El corredor cafetero y su escudería, Prema Racing, terminaron siendo sancionados económicamente por la FIA debido al atuendo de su hermana, Paulina Montoya. El hecho ocurrió en el área del pit lane y garajes. Paulina Montoya acudió a la zona restringida a brindar apoyo a su hermano y se acercó directamente a su monoplaza. Sin embargo, llevaba puesto un vestido corto que no cubría completamente sus piernas. De acuerdo con el Reglamento Deportivo de la categoría (Artículo 22.15) y las normativas de seguridad en pista, toda persona con acceso a estas áreas activas de trabajo debe portar pantalón largo y calzado adecuado como medida de protección industrial frente a combustibles, neumáticos a altas temperaturas y fluidos de los vehículos. Al detectarse la infracción, la escudería Prema argumentó ante los comisarios de la FIA que Paulina no formaba parte del personal operativo del equipo, sino que asistía en calidad de invitada. No obstante, las autoridades fueron contundentes al ratificar la sanción: los equipos son legalmente responsables de la conducta, seguridad y vestimenta de cualquier persona a la que otorguen acceso o acreditación en las zonas restringidas. Por ello, la multa económica debió ser asumida de manera directa por la estructura. Esta particular penalización extraportiva de 500 euros se sumó a un complejo panorama en pista para el piloto colombiano: Aunque el descuido de su hermana no implicó pérdida de puntos en el campeonato ni sanciones deportivas en el tiempo de vuelta, queda como una de las anécdotas reglamentarias más curiosas de la temporada.

articles.title: Haaland goal sees 10-man City beat United in controversial Manchester derby
articles.summary: Phil Foden is sent off for City, but Erling Haaland’s controversial goal settles Manchester derby 1-0 at United.
articles.body:
Erling Haaland has fired 10-man Manchester City to a memorable 1-0 victory over Manchester United despite Phil Foden’s first-half red card to extend a perfect start to manager Enzo Maresca’s reign.

Foden kicked out at United captain Bruno Fernandes on 23 minutes to give the visitors a mountain to climb.

But a new-look City were up to the challenge as the near 250 million-pound ($340m) midfield pairing of Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernandez proved their worth.

Haaland’s winner was laced with controversy as Fernandez was deemed not to be interfering with play when he attempted to head in before the ball reached the Norwegian.

Defeat compounds a miserable Premier League start for United as they are already eight points adrift of City and defending football champions Arsenal.

By contrast, victory was a huge statement for Maresca to quell fears of a major drop-off from City following Pep Guardiola’s trophy-laden decade in charge.

A fervent pre-match atmosphere was fuelled just as much by United fans’ anger towards their own club as it was by the usual animosity between the supporters.

A crackdown on ticket touting in recent months has resulted in widespread condemnation from supporters’ groups after many innocent people faced the threat of sanction.

A normal array of banners and flags in the Stretford End was replaced by just one bearing the message: “The way you treat us is a disgrace.”

The visitors had made the better start in the opening quarter, but looked to have been completely undone by Foden’s ill discipline.

City will argue Fernandes should also have seen red as he fouled Foden and then kicked him in the back.

But there was little case for Foden’s defence as he retaliated by throwing both legs up into Fernandes’s midriff.

Kobbie Mainoo blocked Rayan Cherki’s goal-bound effort before Youri Tielemans nearly sliced Antoine Semenyo’s cross into his own net as City continued to be the more threatening.

Marcus Rashford was inches away from his first United goal since December 2024 when his free kick came crashing back off the post with United’s best effort before the break.

The woodwork came to City’s rescue again just after half-time, when Mainoo curled onto the post from distance and the ball rebounded kindly into Gianluigi Donnarumma’s grasp.

But the City sucker punch arrived on the hour mark.

Haaland adjusted his body brilliantly to sweep in Josko Gvardiol’s deflected cross.

A VAR review deemed Haaland was onside and that Fernandez was not interfering as he stooped to try and head in himself.

City came close to landing the telling blow when Fernandez’s effort was turned onto the post by Senne Lammens.

Haaland also should have had a second when he got onto Fernandez’s wicked low free-kick delivery.

City, though, were not made to pay for failing to add a second as United lacked the composure and quality to make the man advantage count until the final minute of stoppage time.

Fernandes’s reverse ball perfectly picked out Bryan Mbeumo, but he was denied by a fine save from Donnarumma.

Maresca scampered down the touchline in delight at full time.

After a battle for the title went down to the final week of last season, Arsenal and City look a class apart from the competition once more.

Both are locked on 12 points with Chelsea, Liverpool and United already cut adrift.

articles.title: Nick Saban wants a different criteria for judging which teams reach the College Football Playoff
articles.summary: Nick Saban urged a strength of schedule overhaul on "College GameDay" before Oregon's shocking upset and Texas' fourth quarter comeback over Ohio State.
articles.body: If you thought Week 1 of the college football season was wild, Week 2 took the typical chaos to a whole new level. Out of nowhere, the Oregon Ducks suffered a shocking upset on the road to the recently hapless Oklahoma State Cowboys. The Michigan Wolverines, who dropped out of the Top 25 after a disappointing "win" over Western Michigan, and seemed eliminated from contention for the College Football Playoff, beat the No. 11 Oklahoma Sooners. The game of the week delivered, in spades, with the Texas Longhorns completing a remarkable fourth quarter comeback at home against the Ohio State Buckeyes. The Buckeyes dominated the game for 45 minutes, had opportunity after opportunity to put the Longhorns away, and missed all of them. COLLEGE FOOTBALL’S CHAOS ERA IS HERE: TEXAS RALLIES, OREGON FALLS AND LANE KIFFIN EYES RETURN TO OLE MISS Even Texas Tech, which seemed set up to run through an easy schedule, struggled on the road against Oregon State before pulling away late in the fourth quarter. Mostly, the week served as a reminder of what makes college football great: big-name teams playing other big-name teams in incredible environments at historic stadiums. The inherently lesser talent at the collegiate level making come-from-behind wins more possible. And stakes, with wins and losses that matter. It was also a reminder that in the era of the expanded College Football Playoff, these games are becoming less and less common. Because of misplaced incentives, the rise of superconferences, and a selection committee whose criteria for picking teams are nebulous and ever-shifting at best, and bewildering and incomprehensible at worst. Legendary head coach Nick Saban, speaking on ESPN's "College GameDay" on Saturday, had some suggestions on how to improve the playoff process and encourage more of these matchups: strength of schedule. "Players love to play in big games," Saban said. "That’s what great competitors love to do. Fans love to see big games." "I think what we’ve created now is a system of how many games you win helps you get into playoffs, and the playoffs become the barometer for the success of your program," he continued. "We need a better metric to actually evaluate quality wins and quality losses. Some losses are better than some wins." That's become a familiar suggestion, particularly from SEC supporters as it moves to nine conference games, guaranteeing an additional eight losses per season spread around the conference. It also makes some obvious sense. Of course, Ohio State shouldn't be punished much for losing to Texas, and that result should carry more weight than a win over Youngstown State. But this mentality is an accidental argument for the type of evaluation that was used in the BCS era, which fans and many coaches eventually hated. Humans have subjective biases or preferences, and they incorporate those biases and preferences into their rankings. Efficiency-driven rankings do have subjective opinions baked into their underlying model assumptions, but that's less subject to on-field, "eye test" bias than poll rankings. Still, a blend of success rate and efficiency-based computer-driven rankings and strength-of-resume results might create exactly the system Saban wants. Though it might not create the results he expects. The 2025 Alabama season is an ideal example. They weren't punished for a blowout loss to the Georgia Bulldogs in the SEC Championship Game. Though they should have been. Not just because of the outcome, but because of how it happened, particularly considering their full season resume. Their strength of resume was 19th. They weren't a playoff team, considering their performance against their schedule. Would Saban still be happy with the rankings if it hurts his former team? The result of this year's Texas-Ohio State game is another fantastic example. By postgame win expectancy, the game was effectively a draw. Texas had a 50.2% win expectancy, with an adjusted scoring margin of 0.0. The teams were nearly identical. In SP+, Ohio State ranks second; Texas ranks sixth, even after the win. Because schedules themselves are subjective, what you value and how you value it, is also subjective. Especially in the NIL/transfer portal era. articles.title: Liverpool want deal for £30m Italian midfield sensation
articles.summary: Liverpool are eyeing potential midfield upgrades.The Reds declined to add a new midfield option in the summer transfer window. Money was instead spent elsewh...
articles.body:
Liverpool are eyeing potential midfield upgrades.

The Reds declined to add a new midfield option in the summer transfer window. Money was instead spent elsewhere - leaving Andoni Iraola relying on the same cast of characters in the middle third.

The Basque tactico has been searching for the right formula with Alexis Mac Allister , Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai sharing duties in the middle.

Now it's emerged that a promising young Italian international is very much on the radar - with Caught Offside claiming the Merseysiders alongside Aston Villa as well as Inter Milan and Juventus are tracking Fiorentina star Cher Ndour.

The former Paris Saint-Germain player has recently broken into the international picture - and is expected to lead the rebuild of the Azzurri in the coming years.

He had spells at Brescia, Atalanta and Benfica in his younger days before joining PSG and enjoying loans at Braga and Besiktas. It was in 2025 that he finally put down his roots with La Viola - earning rave reviews since then.

Fiorentina want €30m to €35m (£26m to £30m) for Ndour

"Liverpool are seeking a long-term, athletic profile to strengthen their midfield rotation," the report reads.

"Liverpool and Villa value his athleticism for high-tempo systems, while Inter and Juventus see him as a tall, technically gifted local talent suited to Serie A dynamics.

"While his market value is estimated at €20M, Fiorentina are said to demand €30–35M."

Cher Ndour is a 22-year-old, 1.90m Italian midfielder, born in Brescia and eligible for Senegal through his family. A PSG academy graduate who also had loans at Braga and Beşiktaş, he joined Fiorentina permanently in February 2025 for around €5m.

A tall, athletic and technically clean central midfielder, Ndour can operate as a No. 8, deeper controller or advanced midfield option. He offers ball-carrying power, passing range and defensive coverage, although his final-third output and consistency remain areas for development.

Ndour is under contract at Fiorentina until June 2029, giving the club a strong negotiating position and leaving no immediate renewal pressure.

He has started the 2026–27 season in the rotation, with regular early-season minutes suggesting Fiorentina view him as a developing first-team asset rather than a player being actively marketed. No concrete exit appears imminent.

articles.title: Jets Dominate Titans 23-10 as Geno Smith Leads New York to Strong Start
articles.summary: The New York Jets opened the 2026 season in impressive fashion Sunday, defeating the Tennessee Titans 23-10 in Nashville and giving new head coach Aaron Glen...
articles.body:
The New York Jets opened the 2026 season in impressive fashion Sunday, defeating the Tennessee Titans 23-10 in Nashville and giving new head coach Aaron Glenn a victory in his first regular-season game.

The Jets controlled the game for much of the afternoon, especially on the ground and defensively. New York finished with 367 total yards while holding Tennessee to just 195 yards , dominating time of possession for nearly 39 minutes.

Making his first start for the Jets since 2016, Geno Smith delivered exactly what New York needed. Smith completed 19 of 24 passes for 215 yards without throwing an interception or losing a fumble.

He connected with Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell on several big plays, helping the Jets consistently move the football. Mitchell came up with a 40-yard reception that helped set up a scoring opportunity.

The Jets also got a huge performance from Breece Hall . The running back rushed for 102 yards and a touchdown on 22 carries , giving New York a consistent presence on the ground.

New York's defense made life extremely difficult for Titans quarterback Cam Ward . The rookie quarterback finished with only 140 passing yards , and the Jets recorded three sacks.

Tennessee struggled to create much offensively throughout the game. The Titans managed only a field goal early before finally reaching the end zone late, when Ward connected with Elic Ayomanor for a touchdown.

The Jets also got an early boost from rookie tight end Kenyon Sadiq, who scored New York's first touchdown of the season on a three-yard rushing play.

There was one concerning moment for New York, as rookie wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. left with an ankle injury after making a 30-yard catch. Safety Minkah Fitzpatrick also suffered a groin injury and was unable to finish the game.

Still, the Jets walked out of Nashville with a convincing 23-10 victory .

For a team looking to put last season's struggles behind it, the opening performance was exactly the kind of statement New York needed.

articles.title: Inside Greg Luca's AP Top 25 ballot: How two weeks reshaped conference races
articles.summary: Texas vaulted to No. 1 with Saturday's win over Ohio State, marking the unofficial end of the nonconference season and revealing a new set of title contender...
articles.body:
With Hollywood Smothers' plunge into the end zone to complete Texas' rally past Ohio State and vault the Longhorns to No. 1 in the AP Top 25, the nonconference portion of the 2026 college football calendar was just about put to bed.

Texas' 24-23 win over Ohio State in a top-five showdown Saturday in Austin was by far the most noteworthy matchup in a mundane nonconference slate nationally, as most programs opted for easy tuneups over real competition.

Difference from AP poll results in parentheses

Still, the first two weeks offered plenty of opportunity to recalibrate expectations for the championship chases ahead.

Through each week of my debut season with an AP Top 25 ballot, we'll take you inside my thought process behind the picks, with a focus this week on handicapping the contenders in each league.

Texas is the easy pick at the top of the SEC and the national poll, boasting as much talent as any team in the country and validating it Saturday with the most impressive win of the year.

But Georgia has quietly built a strong case for No. 1, too, with an unmatched consistency making up for a lack of explosiveness.

Plenty of other contenders will be heard from, with LSU, Ole Miss, Texas A&M and Alabama claiming spots 7 through 10 in the top 25. My personal rankings have Ole Miss last in that quartet, with Tennessee not far behind at No. 12. Not surprisingly, the SEC race will be crowded.

If we accept the obvious reality that home field advantage matters, then Ohio State losing by the slimmest margin on the road to a top-five opponent should keep the Buckeyes in the mix for No. 1, right?

Of course, respecting head-to-head is important, and the Longhorns are a deserving No. 1. But I kept Ohio State at No. 4 with Indiana at No. 6, and the poll results had those two flipped.

IU's opening win over North Texas looks a little better after UNT routed UNLV on Saturday, but the Hoosiers still have more to prove on defense relative to the Buckeyes.

I had Penn State, USC and Oregon bunched up from No. 13 to No. 16, but many of the other voters were quicker to lose faith in the Ducks after Saturday's loss at Oklahoma State, as Oregon fell to No. 21.

That puts Oregon seventh in the Big Ten, also behind No. 18 Iowa (who I was still not compelled to rank after a 16-13 escape at home against Iowa State) and No. 19 Michigan (which might've lost to Western Michigan in Week 1).

That's far too low for my taste given Oregon's talent and metrics that remain pretty solid.

BYU has appropriately vaulted past Texas Tech as the highest-ranked team in the Big 12 after posting a decisive 28-17 win against an Arizona group on the fringe of the top 25.

Still, the Red Raiders remain correctly listed as the betting favorite because of a much easier schedule, even after Texas Tech looked lackluster in wins against Abilene Christian and Oregon State.

Tech's toughest matchup the rest of the way might be this week's home date with No. 22 Houston, while BYU has to visit to No. 17 Utah for their rivalry matchup in November.

Miami is the runaway favorite by any measure, showing little cause for concern in two blowout wins to open the year.

The more interesting question is who will emerge as the Hurricanes' title game challenger?

The AP consensus would suggest No. 16 SMU is the favorite, ahead of No. 23 Louisville. I'd have those rankings flipped, putting Louisville at No. 20 and SMU at No. 23 on my ballot.

Mustangs quarterback Kevin Jennings is too volatile and turnover-prone, and SMU's defense isn't stout enough to cover for his mistakes.

Louisville should only get better as Lincoln Kienholz settles into the starting job. The difference between his first half and second half in the opener against Ole Miss points that direction.

Boise State continues to look like the clear favorite for the G6 playoff berth, checking in at an unofficial No. 28 in the top 25 votes tally.

Five programs at the Group of Six level landed votes this week, but I'm not ready to put any of them on my ballot. Boise State has the strongest statistical profile in the G6, but even the Broncos rank No. 48 in SP+ and No. 36 in ESPN's FPI. Considering them one of the best 25 teams in the country is wishful thinking.

articles.summary: Browns rookie KC Concepcion posted four receptions and five targets, both team highs, in Week 1
articles.body:
Cleveland Browns rookie wide receiver KC Concepcion posted four receptions for 43 yards on five targets in Week 1 against the Detroit Lions in his NFL debut.

Huddle Up: Concepcion led the team with four receptions, with only backup running back Raheim Sanders seeing three catches as a safety valve. Concepcion also led the team in targets. It's early, but he and fellow rookie draft pick Denzel Boston look like a couple of solid young building blocks. However, treat Concepcion as more of a WR4 or flex fantasy option at this point, with more value in long-term keeper formats.

articles.title: Oregon Ducks' national title odds drop, just inside top 10
articles.summary: Oregon's 39-31 loss to Oklahoma State was crushing, both for the team and for their national title odds.
articles.body:
While it may seem like the world is falling for the Oregon Ducks after falling 39-31 to the Oklahoma State Cowboys , all of their goals remain in attainable. Of course, they'll have to right the ship after two disappointing showings to begin the year, but the loss to Oklahoma State came in non-conference play. Once the Big Ten schedule begins in two weeks, the Ducks ' loss won't count against them.

So, while Oregon can still rebound and have the season that they aimed to have in the end, that doesn't mean that the betting odds are in their favor. And how could they be? The Ducks were utterly outplayed in every aspect of the game against the Cowboys. Dan Lanning said it himself, that the game could've and maybe should've been a blowout rather than an eight-point loss.

The Ducks' national title odds dropped slightly after their Week 1 showing versus Boise State , but they dropped even further after their loss to Oklahoma State. There was other action around college football as well, with a new favorite emerging at the top.

articles.title: Carolina Panthers vs. Chicago Bears Bears game recap: Everything we know from Week 1
articles.summary: The Bears smashed and dashed their way through the Panthers in a high-octane regular-season opener on Sunday.
articles.body:
No one probably expected to see what we saw at Bank of America Stadium on Sunday, as the Carolina Panthers and Chicago Bears put on the highest-scoring regular-season opener in NFL history. But unfortunately for reigning NFC South champions, it was the reigning NFC North champions who scored a bit more.

Here's everything we know from the Panthers' Week 1 loss to the Bears . . .

Chicago's high-powered offense simply forced Carolina into submission, recording eight touchdowns and 552 total yards. They converted on 10 of their 14 third-down tries and won the possession battle at 34:03 to 25:57.

The NFL's top rushing attack from 2025 carried their success into 2026, as the Bears rushed for 247 yards and five touchdowns on 35 attempts. Running backs D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai led the way, combining for 224 yards and four scores on 28 carries.

Bears quarterback Caleb Williams was surgical in breaking down the Panthers defense, completing 21 of his 29 throws for 269 yards and two touchdowns. He also rushed for 65 yards and two more scores.

With the Panthers down 45-31 at the start of the fourth quarter, receiver Tetairoa McMillan fumbled away what would have been a chain-moving, 21-yard reception. The turnover, courtesy of rookie safety Dillon Thieneman, set the Bears up at their own 39-yard line with 14:40 left in the game.

12 plays later, Williams found wideout Jahdae Brown for a 1-yard touchdown to give Chicago a 52-31 at the 6:27 mark.

WR Jalen Coker : eight receptions, 138 receiving yards, two touchdowns

QB Bryce Young : 23-of-37, 361 passing yards, four touchdowns (one rushing), interception

RB Chuba Hubbard : 10 carries, 49 rushing yards, rushing touchdown, three receptions, 38 receiving yards, receiving touchdown

The Panthers (0-1) will travel to take on the Atlanta Falcons (0-1) in Week 2.

articles.title: Matt Olson had a hilarious NSFW reaction to Garrett Stubbs trying to trick him
articles.summary: Sometimes it can be entertaining when a position player pitches.
articles.body:
The Atlanta Braves easily won Saturday's NL East clash with the Phillies . And as we've grown accustomed to seeing in blowouts, the Phillies resorted to a position player pitching in order to preserve the bullpen.

But hey, sometimes it can be entertaining when a position player takes the mound, and Garrett Stubbs certainly tried his best to mess with Matt Olson .

The Braves first baseman stepped to the plate with Atlanta already up by seven runs. Stubbs' game plan appeared to be pretty standard in this situations: Throw as slowly as possible.

He threw three pitches of 36, 40 and 36 mph. And Olson was laughing after he swung and missed at one. But then Stubbs went for a little velocity change, and take a look at how Olson reacted to it.

With two strikes, Stubbs tried to sneak an 83 mph fastball by Olson, and Olson just narrowly missed taking Stubbs deep on it.

But as Olson was making his way to first to jog out the fly out, we could see a little NSFW message to Stubbs.

Michael Harris II hit a home run off Stubbs a couple at-bats later. The Braves would win, 12-2.

articles.title: What We Learned from Wisconsin’s win over Western Illinois
articles.summary: Concerns linger for the Badgers despite the win.
articles.body:
The Wisconsin Badgers got their first win of the season against Western Illinois Saturday night, but question marks still loom large over the program.

In their 36-9 victory, the Badgers came out strong with a 17-0 start that saw the offensive, defensive, and special team units making plays early. Once both teams settled into the game, however, Wisconsin struggled to continue their early success.

While the victory was never in true doubt for the Badgers, Wisconsin will need to clean up errors across the board before heading into Big Ten play.

Here are three things we learned from Wisconsin's win against the Leathernecks.

Colton Joseph continues shaky start to season

Coming off Wisconsin's blowout loss to Notre Dame in Green Bay, Colton Joseph needed a strong showing against Western Illinois. Unfortunately for the Badgers, it was more of the same inconsistencies from Joseph that disrupted the offense at times.

Joseph's carries dropped from 10 against the Fighting Irish to four against the Leathernecks, allowing him to focus on getting yards through the air. And while he did have some explosive throws, including a 55-yard connection with leading receiver Tyrell Henry , Joseph also had accuracy troubles throughout the game. Joseph had multiple throws to relatively open receivers that he simply missed, stalling drives and forcing the Badgers to settle.

One such case came early in the first quarter. With the Badgers just outside the 10-yard line and looking to score on third down, Joseph flew the ball over tight end Jacob Harris 's head, forcing Wisconsin to kick the field goal.

One note that might ease the minds of Badgers fans is that, despite Joseph's shaky start, his experience brings versatility to Wisconsin's offense that simply wasn't present last season.

Joseph will need to correct his accuracy errors quickly, as Big Ten defenses will be more likely to capitalize off his mistakes. But after a 2025 season where a Badger quarterback threw for 200+ yards only once all year, Joseph is a breath of fresh air for this Wisconsin offense.

The Badgers run defense stumbled against Notre Dame, especially in the second half of the contest, but at times showed signs of a unit capable of getting stops.

Against Western Illinois, however, Wisconsin simply couldn't contain the Leathernecks on the ground. Western Illinois rushed for 158 yards, a concerning statistic when looking ahead to the rushing attacks that Wisconsin will encounter later in the year.

In particular, quarterback Kennedy McGill took advantage of his mobility, rushing 18 times for 88 yards and extending drives for Western Illinois. Wisconsin looked one step behind McGill, not being prepared for his designed and improvised rushes.

Despite not allowing any touchdowns in the game, Wisconsin's defense let Western Illinois power drives through the rushing attack. One drive in particular saw the Leathernecks rush for seven consecutive plays and eventually kick a field goal.

Wisconsin's defense was undoubtedly the better unit in 2025, keeping the Badgers in games with a makeshift offense. But for the win total to improve in 2026, the defense will need to make sure winning in the trenches isn't a point of weakness.

Tyrell Henry is emerging in his increased role

Entering the 2026 season, the wide receiver group was a point of focus for many. There was no true standout option coming out of camp, with incoming transfers and tenured Badgers making up the bunch.

While there hasn't been a receiver who's claimed the title of WR1 just yet, Henry has proved to be productive for Joseph and the Badgers through two games. His four catches and 91 yards against Western Illinois led all Badgers, with Joseph targeting Henry nine times throughout the contest.

Even though Malachi Coleman got all the attention with his dazzling route and touchdown catch against Notre Dame, Henry wasn't far behind Coleman in terms of productivity. The fifth-year wideout reeled in four catches for 42 yards against the Fighting Irish, already besting his highs from 2025.

Henry possesses good size and can generate yards after the catch, as seen in his 55-yard play with Joseph mentioned earlier. Based on his activity from these first two games, it seems as if Henry will be a major contributor to the pass game moving forward.

articles.title: Alec Bohm hits tie-breaking, 2-run double in 7-run 8th as Phillies beat Braves 9-4 and avoid sweep
articles.summary: Alec Bohm hit a tie-breaking, two-run double in a seven-run eighth inning and the Philadelphia Phillies beat the Atlanta Braves 9-4 on Sunday to avoid being...
articles.body:
ATLANTA (AP) — Alec Bohm hit a tie-breaking, two-run double in a seven-run eighth inning and the Philadelphia Phillies beat the Atlanta Braves 9-4 on Sunday to avoid being swept in the key NL East series.

J.T. Realmuto drove in three runs on three hits, including a two-run homer.

Bohm's double to center field off Dylan Lee (6-1) drove in Trea Turner and Bryce Harper , who reached on his second double of the game. Bryson Stott and Realmuto had run-scoring singles and Kyle Schwarber 's single off Victor Mederos drove in two more runs in the big inning.

Matt Olson hit a two-run homer off Tanner Banks, who was activated off the 60-day injured list before the game, in the ninth.

Despite avoiding the sweep, the Phillies lost ground to the first-place Braves in the series. After trailing by four games at the start of the series, the Phillies left Atlanta five games out of first place. The Braves won the opener 6-5 in 11 innings on Friday night before rolling to a 12-2 win on Saturday night.

Phillies right-hander Andrew Painter gave up one run six hits and four walks. He pitched out of a bases-loaded jam in the fourth. After walking Austin Riley and Ha-Seong Kim and giving up a single to Michael Harris II , Painter coaxed a popup from Ronald Acuña Jr. and ended the inning on Olson's grounder to first base.

Harris, who had three hits, led off the seventh with a single off left-hander José Alvarado (4-3) and moved to second on a wild pitch before scoring on Olson's single to left field for a 2-2 tie.

Phillies: Following an off day on Monday, LHP Cristopher Sánchez (17-5, 2.79 ERA) is scheduled to start in Tuesday night's opener of a series at Washington.

Braves: RHP Reynaldo López (4-4, 4.13) is scheduled to start on Monday night at the Chicago Cubs .

articles.title: Chicago Bears open with a 50 Burger to beat the Carolina Panthers
articles.summary: The Bears opened a record-setting Week 1 with a huge win over the Panthers. More here from @wiltfongjr.
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears opened the 2026 season playing exactly as many fans figured they would: with an OMG offense and a WTF defense.

On this day, Chicago's offense was good enough as they set a Week 1 franchise record with 59 points, but the defense allowed the Panthers 37.

This was the highest-scoring season opener in NFL history.

The first half featured several momentum swings, with an early Bears fumble leading to Carolina points. Chicago bounced back with 21 unanswered points before Carolina settled down to tie it up, which was aided by a failed Bears fourth-down attempt from their own 21-yard line.

They traded field goals until the Bears drove down in the waning seconds for a 29-yard Caleb Williams touchdown scramble to give the Bears a 31 – 24 lead.

A Malik Muhammad II interception ensured that score would hold as they headed into the locker room.

So if you bet the over, you cashed that ticket in the first half!

The second half started with three and outs from each team, before Carolina drove down to tie it up on a Chuba Hubbard TD run.

The Bears answered with a solid drive, helped by a Carolina roughing-the-passer penalty, which was capped off by a D'Andre Swift TD run.

Chicago's defense held the Panthers on a fourth-down try… and THEN THIS HAPPENED!

Bears offense goes over 50 points on a short Caleb Williams-to-Jahdae Walker TD.

The Panthers answered with a touchdown, but the Bears answered that with an answer of their own with another Swift rushing touchdown.

Share your thoughts on the Bears' Week 1 win in the comments.

articles.title: India win Women’s Asia Cup but do not accept trophy
articles.summary: India were not present at the trophy ceremony, which was led by Pakistani Interior Minister and ACC President Naqvi.
articles.body:
The presentation ceremony for the Women’s Asia Cup cricket final in Dubai turned controversial after winners India refused to accept the trophy from the Asian Cricket Council (ACC) President Mohsin Naqvi, who also serves as Pakistan’s interior minister, amid ongoing political tensions between the South Asian neighbours.

India beat Sri Lanka by 72 runs in the final on Sunday to reclaim the crown from the 2024 champions but the post-match ceremony was delayed by more than 45 minutes as players from both sides waited outside their respective dressing rooms.

The match at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium ended close to 9:50pm (17:50 GMT) but the ceremony did not get under way until 10:40pm (18:40 GMT).

Once the temporary stage for the handing over of awards was set up, Naqvi was seen standing alongside other dignitaries as the ceremony began. Match officials were the first to be presented with their medallions before the Sri Lankan players stepped up for their medals.

Sri Lanka captain Chamari Athapaththu received the runners-up award from Naqvi and then proceeded to speak about her team’s performance.

However, no individual awards, including Player of the Match and Player of the Tournament, were handed out, and neither was the Indian team called up to receive its medals or the trophy.

India won the tournament for a record-extending eighth time.

The tournament’s official social media accounts did not post any trophy celebration images.

The Indian Women’s cricket team’s social media account posted a group photo of the team and coaching staff in what appears to be an empty stadium shortly after the conclusion of the award ceremony.

Images and videos posted on social media showed the Indian team and support staff standing in a circle outside their dressing room ahead of the ceremony. They were not seen near the stage once it got under way and no explanation was provided for their absence.

The tournament’s organisers, the ACC, and the Indian cricket board did not respond to Al Jazeera’s request for a comment.

The scene was reminiscent of a similar incident from last September, when India beat Pakistan to win the Men’s Asian Cup at the same venue but refused to accept the trophy from Naqvi , who headed the ACC then, as well.

He is also the chairman of the Pakistan Cricket Board.

Shortly after the row at the men’s final, Devajit Saikia, the chairman of the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI), confirmed that India’s refusal was based on Naqvi’s presence as the leading figure of the ceremony.

“We have decided not to take the Asia Cup trophy from the ACC chairman, who happens to be one of the main [political] leaders of Pakistan,” Saikia then told Indian media.

India-Pakistan relations have been in trouble for years. But they plummeted further after armed attackers killed 26 men in Pahalgam, a tourism site in Indian-administered Kashmir, on April 22, 2025.

The Resistance Front (TRF) , an armed group which demands Kashmir’s independence, claimed responsibility for the attack. India alleges that TRF is a branch of the Pakistan-based armed group, the Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT), an allegation Islamabad denies.

Following the attack, the two countries scaled back diplomatic relations, and India suspended its participation in the Indus Waters Treaty .

On May 7, 2025, India launched multiple missile attacks on sites in Pakistan and Pakistan-administered Kashmir under what it called Operation Sindoor . India said it struck nine sites in Pakistan, which said dozens of civilians were killed.

Three days later, Pakistan launched Operation Bunyan Marsoos , targeting at least six Indian military sites and killing at least five Indians, according to Indian authorities.

On the same day, the two sides reached a ceasefire agreement , which was announced by United States President Donald Trump.

Has the political tension affected India-Pakistan cricket?

Since the May 2025 hostilities, every meeting of the Indian and Pakistani cricket teams – men, women or junior – has been marred by bitterness between both sides.

During the Men’s Asia Cup of 2025, the Indian team did not partake in the customary handshake with their Pakistani counterparts at the pre-match toss and post-match walkoff. The teams met three times in the tournament, which became hugely political due to the players’ hostile behaviour towards each other.

When Pakistan faced India in the ICC Women’s World Cup 2025 in Sri Lanka, the teams steered clear of handshakes and repeated the practice at the ICC Women’s T20 World Cup earlier this year in England, as well as their group-stage match in the Women’s Asia Cup.

Following the Men’s Asia Cup final fiasco, political experts told Al Jazeera the incident seemed “inevitable” under the tense backdrop.

When is the next India vs Pakistan cricket match?

Both countries will participate in the men’s and women’s tournaments at the upcoming Asian Games in Japan.

While the teams are not grouped together in the early stage as they have received direct entry into the knockouts, the possibility of an India vs Pakistan final remains in both competitions.

articles.title: Freddy Peralta, Jonathan Aranda help Rays beat Astros 14-4 to sweep series
articles.summary: Freddy Peralta pitched five hitless innings, and Jonathan Aranda hit two of Tampa Bay's four home runs to help the Rays finish off a three-game sweep of the...
articles.body:
ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. (AP) — Freddy Peralta pitched five hitless innings, and Jonathan Aranda hit two of Tampa Bay 's four home runs to help the Rays finish off a three-game sweep of the Houston Astros with a 14-4 victory on Sunday.

Peralta (9-11) walked three and threw 86 pitches for the Rays, who became the first AL team to reach 90 wins this season. The right-hander won his fourth straight start and has surrendered two runs over his last 23 innings.

Victor Mesa Jr. had three of the Rays' 15 hits. He had a two-run triple in the first inning off Hayden Wesneski (5-2) before scoring on Chandler Simpson 's groundout to give Tampa Bay the lead for good.

Every Rays starter had at least one hit and scored at least one run.

Richie Palacios hit his 10th homer — a three-run shot for a 7-0 lead after shortstop Jeremy Peña dropped a two-out pop-up to extend the third inning.

Aranda hit a one-out solo shot off Enyel De Los Santos in the fourth before adding his 21st home run this season in the seventh — a two-run shot off Ronel Blanco . Nick Fortes hit his fifth homer — a two-run shot in the fifth off Blanco to make it 11-0.

Isaac Paredes hit a two-run homer in the sixth — his 21st — for Houston's first hit. It came against Brody Hopkins, who replaced Peralta in his major league debut and walked Nick Allen on four pitches.

Allen hit his third homer and Nelson Velázquez added his sixth as the pair hit back-to-back solo shots off Casey Legumina in the eighth.

Wesneski gave up seven runs — three earned — on six hits in three innings.

Astros RHP Hunter Brown (5-3, 3.52) starts Tuesday in Houston against the Royals.

Rays RHP Griffin Jax (7-10, 3.99) starts Tuesday against the visiting Athletics.

articles.title: Blue Jays stomp Orioles 8-1 to win series
articles.summary: The hitters couldn’t capitalize, the pitchers couldn’t stop giving up runs
articles.body:
The Orioles and Blue Jays sent their top starters to the mound today as each tried to help his team claim the series win. Dylan Cease was not on his game, but kept the Orioles off the board through the first four innings. Trevor Rogers , on the other hand, looked very good through four innings before falling apart in the fifth. Between the Orioles' offense failing to capitalize, Rogers's fifth-inning funk, and a disastrous relief appearance, it spelled another loss for the Orioles.

Things started off so well. Cease struggled with control from the get-go and walked leadoff batter Dylan Beavers . Pete Alonso singled, then Gunnar Henderson worked the first of his three walks in the game. With the bases loaded and no outs, they were poised for a breakout inning against one of the best pitchers in baseball. They failed.

Coby Mayo started his at-bat 3-0, then saw four more pitches: a called strike and three fouls. On the eighth pitch of the at-bat, Coby took what was called ball four. The call was challenged by the Blue Jays; the ball barely nicked the strike zone.

After that productive but ultimately unsuccessful at-bat, Samuel Basallo and Christian Encarnacion-Strand were the opposite. They struck out too, but looked overmatched (especially Basallo).

Cease threw 33 pitches, which was the only solace in the inning. Rogers, in contrast, needed just 12 pitches in his four-batter first. Vladimir Guerrero Jr. singled to kick off his big day at the plate.

The Blue Jays took the lead in the second inning. Charles McAdoo singled, then stole second base. With one out, Andrés Giménez hit a pop-up to left field. None of Beavers, Encarnacion-Strand, or Henderson could get to it. Encarnacion-Strand made a diving attempt but it deflected off his glove. Beavers got to the ball pretty quickly after it landed, but McAdoo ran all the way and scored easily. It was an interesting choice given it was hardly a given the ball would fall in, but it worked.

The Orioles had another chance in the third inning, when Henderson and Mayo worked back-to-back walks with two outs. But Basallo popped out on the first pitch to end the inning.

Rogers worked around a Guerrero double and a walk in the third, then pitched a 1-2-3 fourth inning. Guerrero had yet to homer at home this season, which is wild. His double came mere feet from breaking his 0-fer. His drought would only last a little bit longer.

In the top of the fifth, the Orioles tied the game. Beavers doubled, then Alonso singled him in to make the score 1-1. It was Alonso's 100th RBI this season, tops in the American League. We like Pete! Henderson followed with another walk, but both he and Alonso were stranded.

Then, the bottom of the fifth. Rogers went from holding his own to falling apart in a matter of moments. He got two easy outs to start off. Next up, George Springer , who homered. Then Guerrero, who hit his first Rogers Centre home run of the year. Then Kazuma Okamoto went deep. Guerrero and Okamoto both homered on a full count. Before you could blink twice, the Orioles were down 4-1.

Cease, who walked five batters but only allowed one run, was out after five innings. Rogers came back for a 1-2-3 sixth. His final pitching line: 6 IP, 7 H, 4 R, 1 BB, 5 K.

After the bullpens took over, the Blue Jays held the Orioles. The Orioles did not hold the Blue Jays.

Beavers singled in the sixth, his third time on base. Coby Mayo picked up his first hit in the seventh. And Leody Taveras singled off tough submariner Tyler Rogers in the eighth. (My daughter, watching along with me: "Why does that guy throw underhand?!")

Craig Albernaz turned to Yaramil Hiraldo after Rogers exited. Just added to the roster today, the idea seemed to be to have him close out the game barring an Orioles comeback (lol) . He pitched a scoreless seventh inning, though it was bumpy. He issued a walk and gave up Guerrero's fourth hit of the game. He returned for the eighth inning and things got very bad.

Nathan Lukes walked, then Hiraldo got the next two batters. He was so close to a non-disaster! But Brandon Valenzuela singled, then Myles Straw walked to load the bases. Relief pitcher Cam Sanders had been warming up and was surely ready to come into the game.

As Straw jogged down to first base, the camera panned to Albernez decidedly doing nothing in the Orioles dugout. Hiraldo, who had thrown 43 pitches and clearly did not have it, was left in to face Boston Bateman . He walked Bateman to make the score 5-1. Finally, Hiraldo was removed.

Sanders came in to face George Springer. Springer hit a line drive to left-center field. It looked like it might hang up for Beavers to catch, but sank as he approached. Beavers kind of waved his glove at the ball as it sailed past him and went to the wall. All three runs scored.

A better outfielder would have caught that ball. But even Beavers should have gotten a glove on it and kept the worst from happening. I like what Beavers has been doing at the plate lately, but his defense remains upsetting. Guerrero was finally retired to end the inning. The damage was one.

The heart of the order attempted a comeback in the top of the ninth. Alonso and Henderson singled back-to-back, but Coby Mayo struck out. The Orioles had pinch-hit for Basallo with Jeremiah Jackson earlier in the game, so Yohel Pozo batted instead. He promptly hit into a game-ending double play.

Orioles lose, 8-1. They now sit at 72-78. Tomorrow, they start a three-game series against the Mets in New York. I expect we'll see Pete Alonso hit his 300th career home run sometime during the series. Something to look forward to.

articles.title: McGreevy’s Arm, Burleson’s Clutch Bat Help St. Louis Cardinals Beat White Sox Sunday
articles.summary: It really should have been expected when you think about it. There was a lack of energy in the stands at Busch Stadium Sunday afternoon as Michael McGreevy t...
articles.body:
It really should have been expected when you think about it. There was a lack of energy in the stands at Busch Stadium Sunday afternoon as Michael McGreevy through the first pitch for the matinee game against the Chicago White Sox . After Saturday's emotional induction of Pujols , Molina and Sherder into the Cardinals Hall of Fame, Sunday's game was anti-climatic at least at the start. Alec Burleson would have something to say about that later, though.

The Chicago White Sox did not take long before they jumped out to an advantage. In the top of the 2nd inning, Benitendi reached with a one-out single. Peters then doubled which gave the White Sox runners at second and third with just one out. Chase Meidroth lifted a sacrifice fly to center for a 1-0 Chicago lead. Fortunately, McGreevy got Colson Montgomery to ground out without allowing any more runs.

While Michael McGreevy was pitching a fine game, his counterpart David Sandlin was even better for the White Sox for the first half of the game. Through the first 5 innings, he was perfect in a baseball sense. No hits, no walks, no baserunners.

Potential trouble reared its head in the top of the 6th inning when Antonacci led off with a triple. Teel then walked giving the White Sox runners at first and third with no outs, but they would not score as McGreevy got Vargas to fly out to short right for the first out. The crucial play was Murakami grounding to Burleson at first base who fired the ball to Bernal at home who got Antonacci out in a rundown for the second out. Benetendi's groundout to second ended the White Sox 6th with no runs scored.

The St. Louis Cardinals FINALLY got their first hit and baserunner with one out in the bottom of the 6th inning when Nathan Church lanced a single to right field. Masyn Winn followed Church's lead by smacking a single of his own to left-center giving St. Louis runners at first and second with just one out. Unfortunately, Bryan Torres struck out on a high fastball for the second out. What looked like it would be an inning-ending groundout from Herrera turned into an opportunity as it went off the glove of White Sox shortstop Colson Montgomery allowing him to reach and loading the bases. That caused the White Sox to bring in Chris Murphy from the bullpen to face Alec Burleson . Burly proved clutch as he muscled a double into the right field corner scoring three for the Cardinals giving them their first lead of the game at 3-1.

Michael McGreevy gave the Cardinals a great effort Sunday. He pitched 6 innings allowing just 1 earned run while striking out 6 and walking 3.

Gordon Graceffo took over in the top of the 7th inning to begin another St. Louis bullpen adventure. He had no troubles setting the White Sox down 1-2-3 to keep the Cardinals lead preserved at 3-1. After the Cardinals failed to add to their lead in the bottom of the 7th, Gordon was the Cardinals answer for the top of the 8th inning also. He once again had an efficient and drama-free 1-2-3 half-inning.

More than a few of us wanted the Cardinals to add to their 2-run lead in the bottom of the 8th. Nathan Church got that off to a good start as he led off with a double to left-center. The White Sox then turned to Trevor Richards to keep them within striking distance. Masyn Winn did his part by at least flying out to deep right to move Church to third with just one out. Victor Scott II also did his job by lifting a fly ball to right-center deep enough to be a sacrifice fly, but Church failed to tag up and did not score. Unbelievable . After Herrera grounded out to end the Cardinals 8th, you couldn't help but wonder if that mental error would end up being costly.

The top of the 9th would be in the hands of George Soriano to hold this Cardinals lead and give them a series win. His first pitch was hit for a single into left by Vargas. You just knew that the potential tying run would come up, didn't you? After Soriano walked Murakami, the potential go-ahead run came to the plate for the White Sox in the form of Benetendi. All he could manage was a weak flyball to center that didn't advance either runner. Peters grounded out for the 2nd out bringing up Meidroth. Soriano walked him to load the bases and put the potential tying run at 2nd base with the go-ahead run at first. Montgomery, with 31 home runs for the season, stepped to the plate. He mercifully flied out to center on a 2-2 pitch to end the game. It's never easy with this bullpen, but we'll take it.

The St. Louis Cardinals begin a 3-game series against the San Francisco Giants Monday night at Busch Stadium. Quinn Mathews takes the mound for the Cardinals while the Giants have yet to announce a starter. First pitch is scheduled for 6:45pm central time and the game broadcast will be available via Cardinals.tv.

articles.title: BCIB Takes His Braves Scattered, Diced, and Smothered: Phillies 9, Braves 4
articles.summary: Am I allowed to do a Waffle House title if I’ve never eaten at one?
articles.body:
It's not quite true that all's well that ends well, given that the good ending to this series in no way erases the fact that the Phillies lost said series. But it is true that batting around against a hated rival is really, really fun.

Trea Turner got the Phillies' first hit on a little bloop, coming against Atlanta starter Grant Holmes ; it didn't look great coming off the bat, but it landed safely— Atlanta, being home to the country's busiest airport, is used to safe landings. But not all landings are so smooth: Bryce Harper lined a ball to left, and that one did look good off the bat, but Maurcio Dubón dove to snatch it away. Another dive, this one from Matt Olson , took a hit away from Luis Arraez , and the Phillies ended the first without a run.

The Braves got started fast against Andrew Painter with a single from Michael Harris II and another from Olson; the latter of the two put his ball right up the middle. A sacrifice fly from Drake Baldwin put the Braves on the scoreboard first. The Phillies would not take long to respond: Bryson Stott singled, and while he was erased on a ground ball from Brandon Marsh , the Braves failed to turn the double play which would have ended the inning. This would become highly relevant just one batter later, as J.T. Realmuto saw a high four-seamer and decided to send it even higher, watching it arc and sail into the left-center seats for a 2-1 lead.

They'd keep working in the third, with both Kyle Schwarber and Turner walking to begin the frame, but it came to naught on a lineup and double play. That's some misfortune, and the Phillies would encounter more of it in the bottom fourth, as the Braves used a combination of walks and a single to load the bases with just one away and Ronald Acuña Jr. at the plate. But luck turns, eventually, and Acuña flew out, shallowly enough that no run could score; a great grab from Arraez on an Olson grounder ended the inning.

More good fortune for the Phillies, and of their own making: Realmuto doubled when a ball bounced away from Dubón in left , and Justin Crawford singled to put runners on the corners with none away, ending Holmes' day. But luck turns, sometimes sooner than you'd like. Ray Kerr came in from the bullpen to get the platoon advantage against Schwarber, successfully inducing a double play (3-4); a Turner strikeout ended the inning.

Alex McFarlane replaced Painter to start the sixth (final line: 5 IP, 6 H, 1 ER, 4 BB, 3 K), and worked a 1-2-3 inning. José Alvarado took the seventh, allowing a single to Harris II, then advanced him on a wild pitch. Hey scored an an Olson single, and the game was tied. And then it got worse: another single, then a misaimed ball on an attempt to put out a steal hit Arraez in the hand. Fortunately, Alvarado ended the inning before the Braves could take the lead, but the mood was decidedly sour.

The Phillies got Dylan Lee in the eighth, and Schwarber started things off with a single to right. He was soon sent back to the dugout on a force out, but the Phillies kept rolling, with Harper sending a Lee fastball right into the gap between the range of Olson at first and Mike Yastrzemski in right for a double. An Arraez pop out shifted the mood back to tension. Alec Bohm came to the plate in a tone-setting moment: an out would give the Phillies, already stinging from a seasons' worth of painful losses to Atlanta, a sense of doom. But Bohm saw to it that fatalism would not rule the day: he smacked a pitch into center-right to clear the bases, giving the Phillies a 4-2 lead. He scored himself when Stott hit a single into shallow center. The skies cleared, the clouds vacated their positions. Optimism emerged like the first shoots of spring (or, for a more seasonally appropriate simile, like the first pumpkin spice lattes of fall).

The Braves pulled Lee; his replacement, Victor Mederos , fared no better, as Realmuto knocked one into center for another run. It was then, to quote a baseball great, Deja vu all over again as Schwarber came back to the plate, and got another single to right, scoring two more. Turner got a second chance too, and this time made good, sending one through the right-side gap for a RBI. 9-2, good guys. Mederos departed, and former Phillie Bailey Falter was tasked with getting the third out, doing so on a strikeout of Harper.

The recently returned Tanner Banks took the eighth, and showed no rust, in the eighth, putting three Braves down in order. He showed some in the ninth, allowing a two-run homer to Olson. On another day, in a tighter game, this would have produced enormous dread, despair, dismay. Today it produced no more than mild irritation. There was a bit more trouble, but nothing to write home about. The game concluded soon after.

The Phillies are 83-67. They'll start a series in Washington on Tuesday at 6:45.

articles.title: Refereeing body admits judgement error over Haaland derby winner
articles.summary: The Premier League refereeing body Pro Ref admits an error of judgement in awarding Erling Haaland's winner in the Manchester derby.
articles.body:
The Premier League refereeing body Pro Ref has admitted an "error of judgement" in awarding Erling Haaland 's Manchester City winner against Manchester United .

As City celebrated a remarkable derby victory over Manchester United, there were questions as to whether Haaland's winning goal should have stood in a match fraught with controversy.

The striker scored in the 60th minute at Old Trafford, turning home at the back post from Josko Gvardiol's cross before it was disallowed on the field for offside.

Following intervention from the video assistant referee, the goal was awarded - the Norwegian ruled to have been played onside by Patrick Dorgu 's boot.

But there was debate as to whether the offside Enzo Fernandez , diving at the ball in a more central position than Haaland, was interfering with play.

In a statement, Pro Ref said: "It was established that Enzo Fernandez did not play the ball and therefore that makes any offside offence subjective.

"However, on this occasion, the VAR did not recognise the likely impact of his position and should have recommended an on-field review.

"Contact has been made with Manchester United this evening to acknowledge what we deem is an error of judgement. A review of the incident will take place."

United defender Lisandro Martinez said it was an "injustice" while boss Michael Carrick said he was "confused" by the decision.

The goal came after City had gone down to 10 men in the first half when Phil Foden was shown a straight red card for kicking out at United captain Bruno Fernandes .

Foden was dismissed by referee Michael Oliver on 23 minutes after kicking the midriff of Fernandes while he was on the turf.

Haaland's winning goal - why is it controversial?

When Haaland's goal was ruled out as offside on the field, few questioned the decision as the City striker looked to have drifted beyond United's defensive line.

The lines drawn by the VAR showed Haaland to be onside thanks to Dorgu's boot. But it was the positioning and involvement of Fernandez that left many pundits astounded and unsure if it was a legitimate goal.

Gvardiol's cross took a slight deflection off the boot of Dorgu before finding its way to Haaland at the back post, while Fernandez was clearly attempting a diving header in the middle of the six-yard box but he did not touch the ball.

Fernandez appeared to be in an offside position, ahead of Dorgu's boot, but VAR deemed it to be a legitimate goal as he did not touch the ball while United defender Martinez was also closing in.

The Premier League Match Centre said on X: "VAR checked the referee's call of no goal for offside - and determined that Haaland was in an onside position and recommended that the goal was awarded.

"The VAR also deemed that while in an offside position, Fernandez didn't play the ball."

Dale Johnson, BBC Sport football issues correspondent

The curiosity about this incident is that the goal was initially disallowed for the wrong reason. Haaland was flagged offside when he shouldn't have been.

But as it turned out, the goal should have been ruled out because Fernandez was offside.

There is one key part of the offside law which applies to Fernandez here. A player is offside if they are:

"Clearly attempting to play a ball which is close when this action impacts on an opponent."

Both parts of that clause must be met. It is possible for a player in an offside position to attempt to play a ball and not commit an offence – there must be impact on an opponent too.

As the ball came in, Fernandez threw himself to try to head it, with Martinez directly behind him.

Video assistant referee Matt Donohue should ask himself if Fernandez's action would have influenced Martinez.

In other words: If Fernandez had not jumped for the attempted header, would Martinez have made a different decision over playing the ball?

If the ball had been out of reach for Fernandez, or for Martinez, then there is an argument to give the goal.

And also: There would have been no offside had Fernandez made no attempt to play the ball.

But he did. And as it went just a yard in front of Martinez too, it is very difficult to argue Fernandez did not commit an offside offence.

There is also an argument that the actions of Fernandez influence the positioning of goalkeeper Senne Lammens .

However, the goal was originally ruled out for offside against Haaland - which was incorrect. So that decision had to be overturned.

And then, the VAR should have sent referee Michael Oliver to the monitor for the subjective offence by Fernandez.

It would have created the odd situation where a disallowed goal was reviewed to remain ruled out - but this is what should have happened.

It was a clear offside offence by Fernandez and will go down as a VAR mistake.

Was the VAR too concerned with a possible touch by Fernandez?

If so, did the VAR forget that Fernandez was offside, and not consider the subjective offence? It seems to be the most logical explanation.

A similar thing happened in a game between Arsenal and Brentford in February 2023 when a goal by an offside Christian Norgaard was not disallowed.

Confusion as Man Utd seethe at 'injustice'

With Haaland's goal settling the match, United were unsurprisingly disappointed by the decision.

"I think it was offside," said Martinez. "And what I can't understand is the rules. I want to be calm now, I want to control myself.

"It's so hard because you lose a derby, you lose three points at home, and every season they're [referees] coming to our club, they explain for one hour the rules, and they look so confident with that, and then after [there are] five or six people doing these kind of mistakes in the Premier League - it's unacceptable.

"It's the best league in the world, you have the best teams in the world, the best players in the world, and now we have to go home with this injustice."

United boss Carrick also expressed his confusion.

"We put things in place in the game now, we have people in offices with all the screens for this decision," he said.

"It's more worrying about if that's the interpretation of football now. If that's the interpretation of not interfering in the game now, that's really worrying for me. It's a staggering explanation.

"The decision isn't going to change the season, but it's had a major impact on the game."

Wayne Rooney, part of the BBC's MOTD2 team, said: "Surely it's offside. Martinez is impacted by Fernandez's movement, and he is offside."

Gary Neville said on Sky Sports: "I think we'll see some sort of apology from the referee's association, there's no doubt Fernandez is playing that ball and is trying to put off Martinez. I think it's one they'll recognising they got wrong."

Micah Richards added: "I think it's been a bad day for referees. They got the Foden decision wrong and the Fernandez decision wrong. I think they got it so wrong but I don't think it takes anything away from City's performance."

Meanwhile, City boss Maresca said: "I think it was onside clearly so it's good."

'Just a flick' or 'violent' - should Foden have been sent off?

The goal came after a first half laced with controversy, with Foden shown a straight red for kicking out at midfielder Fernandes.

City midfielder Foden picked up the ball wide on the right-hand side in his own half and was closed down by Fernandes, who tripped him.

Foden then kicked out at the body of the Portuguese midfielder while on the ground and was shown a straight red card by the referee.

Replays showed that Fernandes kicked Foden in the back first, before the England international retaliated.

The incident was checked by the VAR, who confirmed the on-field decision; Fernandes was not shown a card.

Pundits were divided on whether Foden should have seen red and whether Fernandes was the man at fault.

Former Manchester United forward Rooney did not believe it was a red, saying "it was more of a flick or a gesture, than a kick out".

Neville said he was "surprised" Fernandes did not receive a booking for his role while Roy Keane said the fault lay with the Portuguese midfielder.

"Foden gets up and reacts obviously, so he's sent off," he said. "Fernandes catches him and gives him a little kick. I guess it's classed as violent. But Fernandes is the one who is violent here, I don't think Foden should have a red card."

Dale Johnson, BBC Sport's issues correspondent, said: "The referee and VAR would have to deem it violent conduct rather than just petulance from Fernandes.

"The guidance changed some years ago to factor that in, so David Beckham's kick on Diego Simeone in the 1998 World Cup would not result in a sending off today.

"It looked to me like there was little to no contact from Fernandes, and if there was it was limited force and wasn't followed through.

"So Bruno's act would be seen as a yellow card offence, which the VAR obviously can't get involved in."

articles.title: Joint-worst start since 1992 and fan protests - Man Utd's day to forget
articles.summary: Manchester United fans protested inside and outside Old Trafford before Sunday's derby, then saw their team lose to 10-man Manchester City
articles.body:
Sir Jim Ratcliffe cannot have imagined it would be like this.

When Ratcliffe agreed on Christmas Eve 2023 to spend £1.25bn to buy a minority stake in Manchester United , his intention was to restore the ailing club to its past glories.

Sitting in the directors' box at Old Trafford watching United lose 1-0 to a Manchester City side reduced to 10 men midway through the first half was definitely not part of the plan.

Ratcliffe knew major decisions needed to be made in order to slash the club's losses. And he knew they were bound to be unpopular.

But nearly three years on, he presumably felt the green shoots of recovery would be starting to grow by now.

After all, the project chief executive Omar Berrada spoke to staff about in September 2024 was an aspiration to win the Premier League title in 2028. In other words, next season.

On the evidence of this 199th Manchester derby, United are a very long shot to achieve Berrada's target.

At this point, even pacifying the thousands of fans who protested against the club's ownership before the Old Trafford defeat by 10-man City looks beyond them.

United now have four points from their opening four games. It equals their worst start to a Premier League season since 1992-93. Last season under Ruben Amorim, they also had four points from four matches.

Man Utd fans' ownership protests intensify

To be clear, United's fans have - to a greater or lesser degree - protested against the owners since the Glazer family landed £600m-worth of debt on to a previously debt-free club with their leveraged buy-out in 2005.

In their most recent accounts to 31 March, United had an overall debt of £1.3bn, including outstanding transfer fees.

Since then they have refinanced $425m (£314m) worth of bonds at a higher interest rate than they had been previously. They also took an additional $125m (£92.4m) but are yet to explain what the additional funds will be used for.

The club's current financial position will be revealed on 23 September when it publishes its full year accounts to 30 June 2026.

Ratcliffe's involvement promised to change the situation. Yet many fans argue that, if anything, things have got worse.

Ill feeling has spilled over since United launched a ticket-touting investigation in the summer.

Although they have admitted to underestimating the number of fans who shared their account details and toned down some of the threats around season ticket confiscation if supporters failed to respond as requested, United officials defended the investigation.

Last week, they revealed 685 fan accounts had been banned, with a further 464 either sanctioned or warned.

However, United added that "468 cases were resolved after supporters responded with the relevant information. No further action was taken, as the information provided satisfactorily explained the activity identified".

Many match-going fans felt the investigation was an attack on them and decided to use the City game to protest - inside and outside Old Trafford.

Huge numbers with flares gathered outside the ground, heeding a call from the 1958 Group, before making their way through the Munich tunnel under the stadium.

Inside, The Red Army group of fans opted not to bring in their usual banners - instead display a single banner above the players' tunnel stating: "The way you treat us is a disgrace."

It meant the only banners in the stadium were the ones the club had themselves put up.

"Unless our generational match-going support is given a real voice that is actually listened to, the little that remains of our fan culture will soon be gone forever," said The Red Army group in a statement.

"TRA aren't a protest group, we're an 'atmosphere' group but we've never shied away from making our position clear when we believe not doing so would be to the detriment of the interests of match-going supporters."

It was noticeable many songs were sung in direct protest against Ratcliffe, as well as the Glazers.

"We wanted the Glazers out and that will never change," said Steve Compton of the the 1958 Group.

"Ratcliffe came in and gave us a glimmer, but his idea of putting Manchester back in Man Utd couldn't be any further from the truth.

"The club have made many statements, but one thing they haven't done is actually apologise to anyone. We've had hundreds of messages directly - this has affected people's health.

"These are regular Joes, working-class people who are sent an email telling them their ticket's been suspended with no actual evidence. How do you defend something you don't know what you're defending against?"

The 1958 Group's allegation, which has been voiced by other fan groups, contradicts United's own comments on Friday that state they did advise fans what they were being accused of. The club declined to comment on the protests.

There were boos from the home fans at the final whistle, although it was not entirely clear whether the reaction was triggered by their team's performance or the officials over the controversial offside call that confirmed Erling Haaland 's second-half winner should stand.

Since Berrada spoke to staff, United have delivered their worst starts in three decades. Many United supporters feel an overall transfer spend of £148m this summer was not enough after Carrick's mid-season arrival led to an improvement that secured a third-place finish.

"I definitely appreciate the supporters," said Carrick.

"We want to try everything to make them happy. They're everything for this football club. I never take them for granted. I speak about that quite a lot, and it means a lot to me.

"I'm feeling for them today on the back of losing the game. We haven't got as many points as we would have liked at this point, for sure. There's no getting away from that."
authors: Simon Stone - Manchester United reporter at Old Trafford

articles.body:
The refereeing body Pro Ref issued an official statement acknowledging a decisive mistake in the derby played this Sunday at Old Trafford, where Erling Haaland scored the winning goal for Manchester City against Manchester United .

The assistant referee had initially flagged Haaland offside in the 60th minute. Although the striker was onside, the VAR failed to assess Enzo Fernández 's impact on the play, even though he did not touch the ball but influenced the action. Pro Ref clarified that the video assistant referee should have recommended an on-field review, as it was a subjective offside situation.

After analyzing the play, the refereeing body confirmed that it had contacted the Manchester United board directly to admit what they described as an "error in judgment," while also announcing the start of a formal review of the incident.

articles.summary: El analista arbitral de Radio MARCA considera acertada la decisión de Juan Martínez Munuera
articles.body:
En el minuto 82 Juan Martínez Munuera señaló el punto de penalti a favor del Atlético de Madrid. En el programa 'Marcador' de Radio MARCA valoró esta jugada el analista arbitral, Pablo González Fuertes .

"A la altura que Ochieng tiene la mano es penalti. Si hubiera estado más abajo se podría haber valorado la inercia de la acción pero a esa altura no hay más remedio que señalar la pena máxima"
